# Scanning Exceptions

Scanning exceptions let your operators record problems with a roll of film, such as "Fogged film", "Blank roll" or "Torn sprockets". Each exception can just be noted, end the roll, or put the roll on hold. It can also message the customer, either after asking the operator or automatically.

Operators record exceptions against a roll on the **Scanner Station** and in the **Film Development App**. Both follow the same settings.

---

## Where to set them up

1. Go to **Settings → Organization → Film Development → Scanning Exceptions**.
   * Note: The tab is greyed out until **Enable Film Development** is turned on in **Settings → Organization → Film Development → General**.
2. Click **Add exception**.
3. Fill in the details (below) and click **Add exception** to save.

![Scanning Exception List](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/80b32ef9-a8eb-4b06-b1fe-787d9ca2a319.png)

---

## The exception details

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Name** | What operators see on the button, for example "Fogged film". Each name can only be used once in your lab. |
| **Code (optional)** | A short code shown before the name on the button. |
| **Sort order** | Lower numbers are shown first. |
| **Description (optional)** | Shown to operators as a hint. |

---

## What happens when this is recorded

Pick one option for each exception:

| Choice | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Just record it** | The roll carries on to its next stage as normal. |
| **Ends the roll** | The roll leaves the queues and its twin-check number goes back in the pool. |
| **Needs a decision** | The roll is put on hold, out of all queues, until someone releases it. |

If you choose **Ends the roll**, you also pick an **Outcome**: **Blank**, **Damaged**, **Unprocessable** or **Other**. The outcome is saved with the roll.

* Note: Once a roll has ended, it can't be moved on through the stages again.
* Note: A roll on hold goes back to the station it was waiting at once it's released.

![What happens when this is recorded](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/a22c3dce-0a24-47ab-96db-5ff3432e1974.png)

### When every roll on a job ends with an exception

In **Settings → Organization → Film Development → General** you can choose what happens to a job when all of its rolls end with an exception: leave the job open (the default), complete it, or cancel it. The job history shows "All rolls ended by exception". Jobs that still have rolls in progress are left alone.

---

## Customer notification

Each exception can send the customer an email, a text message, or both. Under **Customer notification**, choose from **When this exception is recorded**:

| Choice | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Do nothing** | No message is sent. |
| **Offer to message the customer** | The person recording the exception is asked before anything is sent. |
| **Message the customer automatically** | Sent as soon as the exception is recorded — the operator is not asked. |

Then set up the message:

1. Turn on **Email**, **Text message**, or both.
2. For email, fill in **Email subject** and **Email message**. You can add an address in **Copy to (optional)** to get a copy.
3. For text, fill in **Text message**.
4. Check the **Preview** to see how the message will look.

![Customer Email Section](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/eb905b44-8b48-4b00-aae3-182aa1d6e3dc.png)

### Codes you can use

Codes are swapped for the real details when the message is sent:

* `{{customer_name}}` — the customer's name
* `{{order_number}}` — the order number
* `{{roll_code}}` — the roll's twin-check number
* `{{exception_name}}` — the name of the exception
* `{{organization_name}}` — your lab's name

Emails and texts use the email and text settings you already have in **Settings → Organization → Notify**.

* Note: Customers who have unsubscribed, or whose email address has bounced, are not emailed.
* Note: Every message sent is saved against the roll.
* Note: An automatic message is only sent once, even if the exception is recorded again.

---

## Recording an exception

1. Open the roll on the **Scanner Station** or in the **Film Development App**.
2. Under **Exceptions**, tap the exception.
3. If the exception offers to message the customer, a **Message the customer?** box appears. Tick email and/or text and choose **Send**, or choose **Don't send**.

What happens to the roll then depends on the exception's settings. A roll that ends or goes on hold drops out of the queue.

* Note: Once an exception has been recorded, it can't be removed from the roll.

![Scanner Station with the Exceptions buttons and the Message the customer](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/e80fae27-56eb-4fa6-8cf2-2e1a0de7286d.png)

---

## Turning off and deleting exceptions

* Use the **Active** switch to hide an exception from operators without losing its history. Inactive exceptions show an **Inactive** badge.
* You can only delete an exception that has never been recorded. Otherwise you'll see "This exception has been recorded against twin checks — make it inactive instead."

---

## Summary of Best Practices

* Keep names short and clear. Operators tap them mid-scan.
* Use **Ends the roll** only for rolls that really can't carry on, such as blank film.
* Use **Needs a decision** when someone should check with the customer first.
* Start with **Offer to message the customer**. Switch to automatic once you trust the wording.
* Always check the **Preview** before saving a customer message.
